document.title: Afghanistan: Demarche to Taliban on New Bin Laden Threat (Islama 06863)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Taliban UN envoy Abdul Hakim Mujahid says Mullah Omar is the main reason bin Laden still has sanctuary, that 80% of Taliban officials (including Mullah Mohammad Rabbani) oppose it, and that few Afghans favor his presence. He cites a shared dislike of Iran. The U.S. official asks the Taliban to protect Shiites and the Buddha statues in Bamiyan.

events.description: DCM Eastham met Mujahid and delivered counterterrorism talking points on Bin Laden; Mujahid urged US patience.
State Department conveyed same talking points to Wakil Ahmed, a key Omar assistant, earlier that day.
Mujahid called the Embassy to confirm he had passed the points to Wakil Ahmed.
Bamiyan reportedly fell to the Taliban.
Taliban took Mazar-i-Sharif; Shi'as reportedly killed.
US DCM Alan Eastham delivered counterterrorism talking points to Mujahid; Mujahid urged US patience on bin Ladin.
State Department conversation with Wakil Ahmed using the same talking points.
Mujahid called the Embassy to confirm he had passed the points to Wakil.
Taliban took Mazar-i-Sharif; many Shi'a reportedly killed.
Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the demarche to State.
Mullah Omar ordered that the Bamiyan Buddha statues be protected.

key_claims: Mullah Omar is the key supporter of Bin Laden's continued presence in Afghanistan, while Mujahid claims about 80 percent of Taliban leadership opposes it.
Mujahid said Taliban removed Bin Laden's 'instruments of communication' and warned him against political and press activity, but denied he was under house arrest.
Mujahid said the Taliban consist of '10 separate groups' that will fight each other after the war ends.
The US told the Taliban it would hold them responsible for further Bin Laden-instigated terrorism and reserved the right to self-defense.
The embassy assessed Mujahid as a moderate with limited influence in Kandahar, and that Omar is Bin Laden's main protector.
The DCM urged Taliban protection of Bamiyan Shi'as and Buddha statues; Mujahid said Omar ordered the statues protected.
